chunks: And everything in it (the book) that is narrated from Muhammad ibn Masud Al-Ayyashi, I have transmitted it from Al-Muzaffar ibn Jafar ibn Al-Muzaffar Al-Alawi - may Allah be pleased with him - from Jafar ibn Muhammad ibn Masud, from his father, Abu Al-Nadr Muhammad ibn Masud Al-Ayyashi - may Allah be pleased with him.

key_terms.الْعَلَوِيُّ: Al-Alawi, indicating lineage from the Prophet's family (Ahl al-Bayt)
key_terms.الْمُظَفَّرُ: Al-Muzaffar, a key link in the transmission chain
key_terms.رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: May Allah be pleased with him, a honorific used for narrators
key_terms.مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ مَسْعُودٍ الْعَيَّاشِيُّ: Muhammad ibn Masud Al-Ayyashi, a prominent Shia scholar and narrator

ai.seo_question: How is the transmission chain for Muhammad ibn Masud Al-Ayyashi verified in this text?
ai.summary: This passage exemplifies the rigorous isnad methodology employed by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih*, specifically tracing the transmission of Muhammad ibn Masud al-Ayyashi’s narrations through a distinct lineage to ensure their reliability. By explicitly naming intermediaries like al-Muzaffar ibn Ja’far and highlighting the scholarly status (raḍiya Allāh ‘anhu) of the transmitters, al-Saduq reinforces the chain's integrity within the broader context of Shia hadith authentication.
